subject.title: fix(autoreview): allow safe Python runtime references

question: Are the exact Python expression shapes accepted by this branch narrow enough to be treated as non-secret references in both deleted and added patch content?
rationale: This is a policy decision at the secret-scanning boundary: tests demonstrate enumerated cases but cannot establish the repository's acceptable false-negative tolerance or authorize the new safe grammar.

options.title: Approve narrow grammar
options.body: Accept the AST/token-based classifier as the supported safe-reference boundary after reviewing the allow and reject matrix.

options.title: Reduce accepted shapes
options.body: Limit the first merge to direct attributes and matching mapping lookups, deferring lower-confidence environment, comment, annotation, placeholder, or SQL-counter forms.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Decline the relaxation and require downstream diffs to avoid secret-like Python binding names.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow grammar
recommendation.body: Accept the AST/token-based classifier as the supported safe-reference boundary after reviewing the allow and reject matrix.
